chapters.title: Future Ready Thinking
chapters.learn:
Welcome to Future Ready Thinking! Computational thinking helps us solve tricky puzzles step by step—just like a friendly robot.

Three Super-Powers You Will Use

1. Logical Reasoning – Use clues like balance scales or line positions to figure out what is hidden.
2. Decomposition – Break a big picture into smaller parts (like counting small, medium, and big squares one size at a time).
3. Classification – Group things that share a purpose (like travel vs. communication) and spot the odd one out.

questions.t: Use the clues to find the number each fruit represents.
questions.tip20: Two mangoes together make 20. Share that between them!
hints: Start with the scale that has only one kind of fruit.
Once you know the mango, use it in the second scale.
Two strawberries and an apple make 25. You already know the apple!

steps.t: Two mangoes balance 20, so one mango is 20 ÷ 2 = 10.
An apple and a mango balance 25. The mango is 10, so the apple is 25 − 10 = 15.
Two strawberries and an apple balance 25. Two strawberries = 25 − 15 = 10, so one strawberry is 10 ÷ 2 = 5.

questions.t: How many squares are there in this picture?
hints: Now look for bigger squares made of 4 small ones.
Don’t forget the biggest square around everything.

steps.t: Count the small 1×1 squares: there are 9.

questions.t: Find the one that is different from the others.
hints: Say the name of each picture out loud.
Three pictures belong to the same group. What do they do?
questions.why: Letter, telephone and computer are ways to communicate. The aeroplane is for travel, so C is different.

questions.t: Find the one that is different from the others.
hints: Say the name of each picture out loud.
Three pictures belong to the same group. What do they do?
questions.why: Helicopter, bus and train are used for travel. The television is not, so D is different.

questions.t: Find the one that is different from the others.
hints: Say the name of each picture out loud.
Count how many legs each animal has.
questions.why: Elephant, deer and cow walk on four legs. The hen has two legs, so A is different.

questions.t: Who is first? Use the clues to find each kid's place in the ice cream line. Tap a box to mark it.
questions.say: Clue 1: Anika is not the last. Clue 2: Alisha is in the exact middle. Clue 3: The person with the shortest name is first. Clue 4: Chirag stands right behind Ellie.
clues: Anika is not the last to order.
Alisha ends up in exactly the middle of the line.
The person with the shortest name is first in line.
Chirag is Ellie's big brother, so he stays right behind her.
hints: Start with the clue that gives an exact place: who is in the middle?
Count the letters in each name to find the shortest.
Chirag and Ellie need two places side by side.

steps.t: Clue 2: Alisha is in the exact middle, so she is 3rd.
Clue 3: Zoya has the shortest name (4 letters), so she is 1st.
Clue 4: Chirag is right behind Ellie. Ellie is 4th, Chirag is 5th.
Clue 1: Anika is not last. Only place 2 is left.
